name: Bharath Vishwakarma
biography: Visual Artist currently pursuing Masters Degree in Photography Design at NID. I have been pursuing this medium from the past 6 years, Interested in mix media approaches, exploring supernatural elements, fantasy and docufiction. Imagination and reality intertwine, provoking introspection, emotional resonance, and a sense of wonder are the themes I feature in my work.

blocks.html:
“Yogini” delves into the mystical world of the divine feminine, drawing inspiration from ancient mythology, spirituality, and the timeless wisdom that surrounds the concept of Yogini. Through the medium of 3D environment, I have constructed a virtual landscape that serves as a backdrop for this visual narrative.

The video work explores the multifaceted nature of  Yoginis, celebrating her divine energy, grace, and spiritual transcendence. It seeks to honor the empowered female figures who embody the essence of Yogini, inviting viewers to reflect upon the profound connection between femininity, spirituality, and the natural world.

Through the use of digital technology, I have created a visual language that combines ancient symbolism with contemporary aesthetics. The interplay of light, color, and form evokes a sense of enchantment, guiding viewers through a series of evocative scenes that elicit a range of
emotions, from tranquility and introspection to awe and inspiration.

‘Water space & people’ is an observational documentary. The mode of this video exists on a spectrum between poetic and expository documentary. A city or a community is
formed where the water body is present, which then forms a space, later that space is
turned into an architecture by the people. My work explores the contrast between the
popular and abandoned stepwells, also how we’re using them with respect to tourism.
A Non-linear edit on how the person in the film witnesses these places in a time
loop and later disappears.

Nagoba Jatara is one of the most important Jataras of the Gond and Pardhan tribes of erstwhile Adilabad. The Jatara receives devotees from across Telangana and the adjoining States. Few elder members of the Mesram clan go barefoot to the river Godavari few days before the Jatara, bring holy water and keep it near the Banyan Tree in front of the Nagoba Temple.
Women folk of the Buigota Khandan of Mesram Clan prepare an earthen ‘lingam’ and later make mud balls out of it and arrange them in seven concentric circles one above the other. The mud balls are used to plaster the floor of the Sati shrine on the premises of the Nagoba Temple. The clan priest and village headman prepare seven lumps of mud and decorate them with vermillion paste to make the Sati.
New brides of the clan in white saris come in a procession and enter the Sati shrine and worship the seven miniature stones representing their seven divine ancestors. They are then led by older women to worship the Nagoba, after which they are recognised as full-fledged members of the clan entitled to participate in all socio-religious rituals and rites.
Nagoba has a lengthy legend recited by Pardhan tribal bards in accompaniment of musical instruments for several days. The narration includes many adventures of tribal heroic men and women including long travels to bring rare things, carrying a ‘kalash’ of sacred water of Ganga, observing penance under banyan trees surrounded with anthills, etc. The heirs and predecessors of one Jejkal Dev are said to have passed on the sacred Kalash to their next generations. The Gonds and Pardhans still symbolically observe the legendary practice of worshipping the sacred Kalash kept on the branches of a banyan tree, travelling barefoot for several days to the river Ganga (i.e. Godavari) to fetch sacred water and so on.

blocks.html: Through this project, I would like to show my experiences of loneliness after experiencing love, especially in the absence of the other person involved in the romantic relationship. Reflecting on the thoughts I felt and the experiences of the past are some of the areas of exploration.

The Surprise is a imaginary narrative, made during sound module / NID
Theme - love, tragedy, pain

the rooftop chimera,
The war between thoughts and actions never ceases, and my body tries its best to transcend this war, even as it gets tired day after day... It still tries its best. It seems like madness or laziness to the outer world, but it's actually a fight between presence and existence.
